intro.title: useKeyPress
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useKeyPress` that detects when a specific keyboard key is pressed. You will learn how to use the `useState` and `useEffect` hooks to manage state and handle browser events. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and the native JavaScript `keydown` and `keyup` events. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that can track key presses for interactive features like keyboard shortcuts or game controls.
intro.usecase: The useKeyPress hook is essential for creating keyboard shortcuts in professional applications. In data dashboards, developers use it to navigate between charts with arrow keys or refresh data with F5. Form-intensive applications implement keyboard shortcuts like Ctrl+Enter to submit or Escape to cancel modal dialogs. Interactive tools like design editors rely on key combinations (Ctrl+Z for undo, Ctrl+S for save) to enhance user productivity. Even simple UI components like search filters can benefit from Enter key submission for smoother user workflows.
